messages:
sophia: heads-up — starting nomad9b-int4 onboard on dedicated. smoke looks good for perf but saw a weird quality regression on multilingual prompts that include emoji clusters. wondering if sparse-kv blocking + tokenizer normalization is the culprit.
ajay: can you paste one of the failing prompts + the outputs so we can repro quickly?
sophia: short example: "Hi 🇺🇸🇵🇸 — explain code-switching in 2 sentences."
float16 output (expected): mixes english/arabic correctly.
int4+kv-sparse output (observed): single-line hallucinated claim, dropped Arabic segments.
metrics (quick): float16 ppl=11.9; int4+kv-sparsity=0.25 ppl=13.7; rouge-L down ~6 pts on our small set.
marta: fyi we've seen emoji-run collapse before — our normalizer applies NFKC then BPE. for some long glyph sequences the tokenizer merges into a single token which then produces a single KV entry. with sparse-kv blocking we prune early entries and the prefix alignment drifts. not rotor/rotary-related, more tokenizer + kv sparsity interaction.
ajay: interesting. can you share the tokenizer tokens for the example?
sophia: tokens dump: [U+1F1FA U+1F1F8] [U+1F1F5 U+1F1F8] -> BPE merges into single token id 50298. when repeated (emoji pair + zero-width joiners) we get two identical consecutive tokens which our sparse-KV backend compresses.
yang: does this show up if we disable sparse-kv? might be kv pruning heuristic that assumes unique prefixes.
ajay: quick ab tests i ran locally:
```
# baseline float16
python eval.py --model nomad9b-fp16 --tokenizer nomad-bpe --prompts multilingual_emoji.json --out /tmp/nomad_fp16
# int4 with no kv-sparsity
python eval.py --model nomad9b-int4 --quant int4 --kv-sparsity 0.0 --tokenizer nomad-bpe --prompts multilingual_emoji.json --out /tmp/nomad_int4_nokv
# int4 with kv-sparsity 0.25
python eval.py --model nomad9b-int4 --quant int4 --kv-sparsity 0.25 --tokenizer nomad-bpe --prompts multilingual_emoji.json --out /tmp/nomad_int4_kv25
```
results snippet:
- fp16: ppl 11.9, hyb-rouge 0.74
- int4 no-kv-sparsity: ppl 12.5, hyb-rouge 0.71
- int4 kv-sparsity 0.25: ppl 13.8, hyb-rouge 0.66
so disabling kv-sparsity recovers ~half of the regression.
marta: that matches the tokenizer hypothesis. another angle: some conversions we do (Gemma->Qwen style) change the emoji normalization table ordering which shifts BPE merges. conversion tool might reorder some merges for compression. did we run the tokenmap roundtrip check for nomad9b?
sophia: i did a tokenmap roundtrip but only for ascii/latin ranges. missed emojis.
yang: actionable: 1) add emoji-heavy prompts to the onboarding eval set (multilingual + ZWJ + flag sequences), 2) run tokenmap roundtrip specifically including emoji and ZWJ ranges, 3) test int4 variants with kv-sparsity bucket toggles (0.0, 0.1, 0.25) and adaptive prune disabled.
triage-bot: created ticket INF-9823: "nomad9b-int4: emoji-sequence tokenizer + sparse-KV interaction causing quality regression" (assignee: marta, priority: P2).
ajay: quick mitigation option: add a pre-tokenizer hook to split merged emoji runs into constituent codepoints before BPE — cheap and reversible. we can A/B in the hosted fleet.
marta: i'll run the tokenmap + roundtrip and post the findings here. also will check conversion scripts for reordering heuristics. if we confirm conversion reorder, we need to pin the emoji merge table ordering during model conversion.
sophia: thanks. for now i'll rollback nomad9b-int4 from canary until we have a test that covers the edge-case. leaving the int4 float path in staging.
yang: also adding a small eval that compares KV cache entries between runs (dump num_unique_kv_entries per step) should show the collapse pattern.
ajay: i'll add the kv-entry-diff metric to the eval harness and submit a tiny patch.
sophia: perfect — keeping this thread for the triage notes. please ping me with PRs/links. :thumbsup:
